blocks.heading: The format
lines: A paragraph of about 100 to 150 words and four options. Pick the one that best captures its point.
Multiple choice: +3 right, minus 1 wrong. About 2 minutes each.

blocks.heading: The method
lines: Before the options, write the point in one sentence of your own: who or what, the main claim, and any condition on it.
Find the turn (but, however, yet, in fact). The summary has to keep the side of the turn the author is on.
Read the options and cut, using the list below. Then compare the last two with your own sentence.

blocks.heading: Options to cut
lines: Adds something the paragraph doesn't say: a new cause, a solution, a recommendation.
Changes the scope: some becomes all, may becomes will, one country becomes everywhere.
Keeps only the example or one detail and loses the claim.
Reverses the relation: cause and effect swapped, or the author's view flipped.
Copies many of the paragraph's words but changes one link between them. Check those closely.

blocks.heading: Between the last two
lines: Pick the one that would tell someone who hadn't read the paragraph what it argues.
Prefer the one that keeps the paragraph's limits (in some cases, may, often).
Down to two: answer. Three still possible after 2 minutes: leave it blank.
